title: Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Auditorium on 1969-06-28
lineage: SBD > MR > Cassette > DAT > CD > Kenwood TrueX > EAC > shn V3 (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a classic ’69 set with stellar country numbers and a monster Turn On Your Love Light.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, clear sound—typical of a good soundboard source—though one reviewer notes it still shows the faint need for Dolby noise reduction. Musically the show shines: Jerry’s steel‑guitar work on “Slewfoot” and “Silver Threads”, Pigpen’s soaring “King Bee”, and an epic 27‑minute “Turn On Your Love Light” make this a must‑have classic‑’69 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Eight reviews (six 5‑star, one 4‑star, one 1‑star) overwhelmingly praise both the musical performance and the recording quality; weighted average yields a rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Most listeners describe the sound as crisp, clear and exquisite. One reviewer mentions slight noise‑reduction issues (Dolby), but overall the mix is balanced and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A quintessential 1969 set that leans heavily into American roots material early on, flowing smoothly through country‑flavored numbers before launching into the expansive love‑light jam.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Plays steel guitar on “Slewfoot” and “Silver Threads”, stretches his vocals, and delivers classic pedal work throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as ‘rocking the bass like it’s a baby in his arms’, providing a solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals are called soulful, cutting to the core; praised on country numbers and overall presence.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s double‑drum magic noted as firecracker drums that drive the energetic set.
